questions.question: Which embolisation technique is the programme's default?

positions.position: No completed randomised study compares bland embolisation with conventional TACE, so both are acceptable; drug-eluting embolics are advised against for increased hepatobiliary toxicity in NET.
positions.locator: Gate 7 · Reasonable option 'Bland embolisation or conventional TACE' · when; Gate 3 · Reasonable 'Add a liver-directed procedure…' · note

positions.position: Generally prefers bland embolisation in small-intestine NET.
positions.locator: Gate 7 · Reasonable option 'Bland embolisation or conventional TACE' · caveat; What we are not sure about #14

positions.position: Calls chemoembolisation possibly more effective in functioning pancreatic NET, the opposite lean to ENETS 2024.
positions.locator: Gate 7 · Reasonable option 'Bland embolisation or conventional TACE' · caveat; Gate 3 · Reasonable 'Add a liver-directed procedure…' · note

positions.position: Retrospective 123-patient series: bland embolisation outperformed chemoembolisation on response in carcinoid (81.0% vs 44.4%) without survival difference; islet-cell results trended the other way. Roadmap critique: the referring physician chose technique, so effects are confounded.
positions.locator: Gate 3 · Reasonable 'Add a liver-directed procedure…' · pref and note; Gate 7 · Reasonable option 'Bland embolisation or conventional TACE' · pref; What we are not sure about #14

positions.position: Protocol of the only prospective three-way comparison, still enrolling; it reports no outcome data. Its drug-eluting-bead arm later closed for severe complications, reported in ENETS 2024 rather than the protocol.
positions.locator: What we are not sure about #15; Gate 7 · Avoid 'Avoid drug-eluting embolics in NET.' · note

questions.divergence: NCCN accepts both techniques while ENETS 2024 leans to bland embolisation in small-intestine NET and ENETS 2023 to chemoembolisation in functioning pancreatic NET, and the comparative data are either underpowered or confounded by referral.
questions.proposal: No default is set. Bland embolisation and conventional TACE are both Reasonable (grade C), chosen by burden, symptoms, liver reserve and biliary-infection risk and not treated as interchangeable; drug-eluting embolics are avoided. The roadmap calls the default an expertise-and-availability decision, with technique, goal, hepatic progression-free survival and toxicity recorded for every procedure.
questions.proposal_locator: Gate 7 · Reasonable option 'Bland embolisation or conventional TACE'; Gate 7 · Avoid 'Avoid drug-eluting embolics in NET.' · pref; Gate 7 · flag note; What we are not sure about #14
questions.rationale: The only prospective three-way comparison is still enrolling and its drug-eluting-bead arm closed for severe complications. One small randomised TAE versus TACE trial (Maire 2012, 26 patients, cited from ENETS rather than read in full) found no significant 2-year progression-free survival difference but was underpowered. The best non-randomised comparison favours bland embolisation on response in carcinoid disease (81.0% versus 44.4%, odds ratio 6.41) with no survival difference, but treatment was chosen by the referring physician; ENETS 2024 prefers bland in small-intestine NET while ENETS 2023 calls chemoembolisation possibly more effective in functioning pancreatic NET. Any choice is expertise and availability.
questions.audit: Registry: technique, goal, hepatic progression-free survival, toxicity.

questions.question: Is first-line PRRT offered for receptor-positive grade 2–3 disease, and to whom?

positions.position: Open-label trial in newly diagnosed SSTR-positive GEP-NET with Ki-67 10–55%: progression-free survival 22.8 vs 8.5 months; overall survival immature with 48% crossover. Roadmap grades it B, not A.
positions.locator: Gate 4 · Standard option '177Lu-DOTATATE, well-differentiated G3, receptor-positive' · when; What we are not sure about #7

positions.position: Grades the NETTER-2-based first-line recommendation 1b-A, stronger than the roadmap’s B, and prefers PRRT over targeted agents (2b-B) and chemotherapy (3b-A) on cross-trial comparison.
positions.locator: Gate 4 · Standard option '177Lu-DOTATATE, well-differentiated G3, receptor-positive' · note (pathway data; not in the Word export); Gate 6 · flag note

positions.position: Backed first-line PRRT only for a minority of carefully selected patients (17 of 22 panellists, 77.3%).
positions.locator: Gate 4 · Standard option '177Lu-DOTATATE, well-differentiated G3, receptor-positive' · note; What we are not sure about #7

positions.position: First-line PRRT can be considered in receptor-positive GEP-NET with Ki-67 10–55%.
positions.locator: Quick reference 'Ki-67 thresholds that change the pathway' · row 'Ki-67 10–55%'

questions.divergence: Itanet and NCCN support or permit first-line PRRT while EANM confines it to highly selected patients, and the roadmap downgrades to B because NETTER-2 is open-label with immature survival and narrow entry criteria.
questions.proposal: Standard, grade B, for the phenotype NETTER-2 tested: uptake above normal liver in target disease, Ki-67 10–55%, documented renal, marrow and hepatic reserve, and clinically significant burden (a local criterion). Ki-67 above 55%, receptor-negative or FDG-avid disease and prior liver-directed therapy fall outside the evidence; the B downgrade and who qualifies remain open decisions.
questions.proposal_locator: Gate 4 · Standard option '177Lu-DOTATATE, well-differentiated G3, receptor-positive' · pref and caveat; Gate 6 · flag note
questions.rationale: One open-label randomised trial with a progression-free survival endpoint; overall survival immature. Depends on radiopharmaceutical availability and payer authorisation.
questions.audit: Registry: every PRRT course, progression-free survival, hepatic and renal function.

questions.question: Hepatic burden threshold above which cytoreduction is not attempted.

positions.position: Still prints debulking of more than 90% of metastatic disease for symptom relief and progression-free survival; the roadmap notes the 90% figure began as a symptom-relief observation never validated oncologically.
positions.locator: Quick reference 'Cytoreduction thresholds, and what supports them' · row 'More than 90% of metastatic disease — NCCN'

positions.position: Small-bowel NET: at least 70% of visible liver disease, near consensus with one dissent, resting on two retrospective single-institution series from the centres that championed the lower threshold.
positions.locator: Quick reference 'Cytoreduction thresholds…' · row 'At least 70% of visible liver disease — NANETS 2017, small bowel'; What we are not sure about #1

positions.position: Pancreatic NET: no consensus; over half favoured an individualised target above 70%, some held only complete clearance helps, and a minority doubted any benefit of cytoreduction is established.
positions.locator: Quick reference 'Cytoreduction thresholds…' · row 'More than 70%, individualised — NANETS 2020'

positions.position: 70–90% or more of visible disease with adequate liver function (2b, grade B), with no guidance on which end of the range applies to whom.
positions.locator: Quick reference 'Cytoreduction thresholds…' · row '70–90% or more — ENETS 2023'; Gate 5 · Reasonable 'Operate for meaningful reduction…' · note

positions.position: The 52-patient series cited for 70% excluded patients in whom 70% looked unachievable, so has no sub-70% arm; extent of debulking did not correlate with liver progression-free or disease-specific survival.
positions.locator: Gate 5 · Reasonable 'Operate for meaningful reduction…' · note

questions.divergence: Targets run from more than 90% (NCCN) through 70% (NANETS 2017) and 70–90% (ENETS 2023) to none at all (ENETS 2024, ESMO), and no comparative study supports any of them.
questions.proposal: No percentage is adopted as evidence. Operate only when a named target can be cleared, with the expected residual stated beforehand, in a patient fit for a long operation with enough functional parenchyma; avoid diffuse-miliary disease and liver replacement above roughly 50–70%. The open NELM-R1 proposal uses at least 70% achievable debulking when extrahepatic disease is present.
questions.proposal_locator: What we are not sure about #1; Gate 5 · Reasonable 'Operate for meaningful reduction…' · caveat; Gate 5 · Avoid 'Do not call debulking complete eradication…'; NELM-R1 · proposed position
questions.rationale: Debulking series are single-arm and selection-driven and no threshold is evidence-derived. The 90% figure was an observation about symptom relief, never validated oncologically; the 70% figure was set by consensus on two retrospective series from the championing centres, and the cohort most cited for it excluded by design every patient in whom 70% was unachievable, so it has no sub-70% arm. NANETS 2020 reached no consensus for pancreatic primaries.
questions.audit: Registry: burden before and after, residual, liver progression-free survival.

questions.question: Does the programme offer radioembolisation in this disease at all, and at what point?

positions.position: Permits radioembolisation, especially for lobar or segmental distribution or after Whipple or biliary instrumentation; a mandatory exhaustion-of-all-options rule before Y90 is a local restriction, not NCCN.
positions.locator: Gate 7 · Reasonable option 'Radioembolisation — Y-90 or holmium-166' · when; Gate 7 · flag note; What we are not sure about #31

positions.position: Found no agreement on which embolisation modality to prefer; considered radioembolisation evidence too thin for second line but supported it in later lines for liver-dominant disease.
positions.locator: What we are not sure about #31

positions.position: Ten-centre retrospective series of 148 patients reporting 70-month median survival; the roadmap calls this immature, unstandardised for response and not a treatment effect.
positions.locator: Gate 7 · Reasonable option 'Radioembolisation — Y-90 or holmium-166' · pref; What we are not sure about #17

positions.position: Cirrhosis-like morphology or portal-hypertension signs in 15 of 52 (29%) followed beyond a year, more after bilobar treatment; median survival 28.0 months in 93 patients; no radioembolisation-induced liver failure.
positions.locator: Gate 2 · Avoid 'Do not offer Y90 radioembolisation without a phenotype-specific rationale.' · caveat; Gate 7 · Reasonable option 'Radioembolisation — Y-90 or holmium-166' · caveat; What we are not sure about #17 and #18

positions.position: Adding holmium SIRT to PRRT gave 2-year hepatic progression-free survival 82% vs 50% in 24 matched pairs, without survival benefit; manufacturer-funded; sequencing safety remains unknown either way.
positions.locator: Gate 7 · Reasonable option 'Radioembolisation — Y-90 or holmium-166' · pref; What we are not sure about #19

questions.divergence: NCCN allows earlier radioembolisation for specific anatomy and NANETS reached no modality consensus, while the supporting series are retrospective or historically controlled and the late hepatic-injury risk is real but unquantified.
questions.proposal: Radioembolisation (Y-90 or holmium-166) is Reasonable, grade C and expertise-dependent for selected lobar or segmental liver-dominant disease with a stated rationale, not restricted to last resort; it is avoided in low-burden disease with a long horizon, where cumulative hepatic radiation raises the threshold. Whether the programme offers it at all is unresolved.
questions.proposal_locator: Gate 7 · Reasonable option 'Radioembolisation — Y-90 or holmium-166'; Gate 2 · Avoid 'Do not offer Y90 radioembolisation without a phenotype-specific rationale.'; Gate 7 · flag note
questions.rationale: Evidence is minimal and the long treatment horizon makes cumulative hepatic radiation injury the dominant consideration.
questions.audit: Registry required if offered; long-term hepatic follow-up.

questions.question: Does the programme open a NELM transplant protocol?

positions.position: 5- and 10-year survival 97.2% and 88.8% with transplant vs 50.9% and 22.4% without. Roadmap critique: non-randomised, younger recipients, self-selected controls; adjusted benefit 6.82 months at 5 years.
positions.locator: Gate 9 · Reasonable 'Offer transplantation only within a trial or prospective registry…' · pref and note

positions.position: Same unit: 10-year survival 93% after transplant vs 75% after resection, univariate only, with recipients selected by a test of time; nodal status, absent from Milan criteria, predicted post-transplant survival.
positions.locator: Gate 9 · Reasonable 'Offer transplantation only…' · pref and note; Gate 9 · Avoid 'Do not take the published series' criteria…' · caveat

positions.position: Deems liver transplantation investigational, acknowledging considerable associated risks.
positions.locator: Gate 9 · Reasonable 'Offer transplantation only…' · caveat

positions.position: Reduces transplantation to a rare consideration in selected individuals after primary resection leaves liver-only disease.
positions.locator: Gate 9 · Reasonable 'Where disease is limited enough to clear, compare resection…' · pref

positions.position: NELM is a nonstandard, not standardised, MELD exception; the guidance requires G1/G2 histology with Ki-67 under 20%, a portal-drained GEP primary and six months without recurrence, but states no age limit or hepatic burden cutoff.
positions.locator: Quick reference 'Milan-NET transplant criteria' · OPTN column; What we are not sure about #23 and #24

questions.divergence: The Milan series reports large survival gains that the roadmap judges largely selection-driven, NCCN calls transplantation investigational and ENETS 2024 a rare consideration, so opening a protocol is an institutional judgement on graft stewardship.
questions.proposal: Transplantation only within a trial or prospective registry under restrictive criteria (Reasonable, grade C), via the nonstandard review-board route at MMaT-3, after comparing resection or cytoreduction at the same board; never for G3 or carcinoma, extrahepatic disease, an unresected primary, no observation period or no registry entry. Whether to open the protocol remains undecided.
questions.proposal_locator: Gate 9 · Reasonable 'Offer transplantation only within a trial or prospective registry…'; Gate 9 · Reasonable 'Where disease is limited enough to clear…'; Gate 9 · Avoid 'Do not list G3 disease…' · note
questions.rationale: Non-randomised series: 42 transplanted patients at one centre over 15 years, with recipients 15 years younger, a self-selected comparison arm, a pre-targeted-therapy comparator and 88% marginal grafts; adjustment for measured factors narrowed the benefit to 6.82 months at 5 years and unmeasured selection remains, and 6 of the 9 deaths after transplantation were from transplant sequelae. NCCN still calls transplantation investigational and NELM is a nonstandard exception, not a standardised one. Graft stewardship is an institutional judgement.

questions.question: Who owns carcinoid-crisis prophylaxis, and how is it verified before each procedure?

positions.position: Prophylactic octreotide is likely ineffective at preventing intraoperative carcinoid crisis, yet NCCN preserves short-acting octreotide before embolisation for hormonal syndromes.
positions.locator: Gate 8 · Avoid 'Do not rely on prophylactic octreotide…' · caveat; Gate 8 · Standard 'Give short-acting octreotide before embolisation…' · note

positions.position: Says crisis prevention has not been established while sanctioning an intraoperative octreotide infusion; the roadmap calls this internally conflicted.
positions.locator: Gate 8 · Avoid 'Do not rely on prophylactic octreotide…' · caveat and note

positions.position: Calls the role of analogues in preventing crisis in pancreatic NET undefined.
positions.locator: Gate 8 · Avoid 'Do not rely on prophylactic octreotide…' · caveat

positions.position: Narrative review putting crisis at 1–2% after 177Lu-dotatate and warning that octreotide near a dose can block uptake; its own 127 administrations produced no crisis, and it gives no rule for the trade-off.
positions.locator: Gate 8 · Standard 'Give short-acting octreotide…' · caveat; Gate 8 · Avoid 'Do not rely on prophylactic octreotide…' · note

questions.divergence: Sources agree prophylaxis is unproven but differ on intraoperative octreotide and on incidence (1–2% after PRRT versus 24–30% intraoperative events in surgical series), so the roadmap makes preparedness, not prophylaxis, the safeguard.
questions.proposal: Every functional patient has a written, procedure-specific crisis plan with a named owner, rescue octreotide in the room and immediate haemodynamic treatment (Standard, grade D). The board names the prophylaxis owner separately, prophylaxis is documented before every procedure and audited for adherence, and octreotide near PRRT is decided explicitly with nuclear medicine.
questions.proposal_locator: Gate 8 · Standard 'Write a procedure-specific crisis plan…'; Operations · board meeting · Output; Operations · dashboard · Functional disease; Gate 8 · Standard 'Give short-acting octreotide…' · caveat
questions.rationale: Not an evidence question. It is a named safety process that fails when it lives in individual memory.
questions.audit: Audit: prophylaxis documented before every procedure in functional patients.

questions.question: Re-biopsy policy for suspected grade progression or transformation.

positions.position: Grades re-evaluation before radioligand therapy when behaviour changes 3a-A, stronger than the roadmap’s ‘consider’.
positions.locator: Gate 1 · Reasonable 'Consider re-biopsy on unexpected behavioural change or discordant FDG avidity.' · note

questions.divergence: Itanet supports re-evaluation before radioligand therapy on behavioural change, but no study defines the trigger or interval, which is why the roadmap holds re-biopsy at grade C.
questions.proposal: Consider re-biopsy (Reasonable, grade C) on unexpected behavioural change or discordant FDG avidity, particularly where the original grading is years old or the disease has changed pace, but not as a scheduled ritual; grade is reassessed on any metachronously sampled specimen. Whether re-biopsy becomes a required step before PRRT remains open for local ratification.

questions.question: Is hepatic debulking offered in well-differentiated G3 disease, and under what conditions?

positions.position: Refers grade 3 liver metastases for systemic therapy rather than cytoreduction.
positions.locator: Gate 4 · flag note; What we are not sure about #34

positions.position: Carcinoma should not be resected; localised well-differentiated G3 may be resected within multimodal therapy, with liver cytoreduction often not indicated, while conceding its well-differentiated G3 recommendations are unsupported.
positions.locator: Gate 4 · flag note; What we are not sure about #34

positions.locator: What we are not sure about #34; Gate 4 · Standard 'Poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma: platinum–etoposide…' · caveat

positions.position: Allows the whole G1–G2 menu in G3 disease on informal consensus rated very low quality, and supports no Ki-67 cutoff.
positions.locator: What we are not sure about #34

positions.position: Gives this phenotype the strongest randomised systemic evidence on the page, which is why the surgical question will reach the board; it does not address surgery.

questions.divergence: Both NANETS papers lean against G3 liver cytoreduction but NANETS 2020 calls its own G3 advice unsupported, ENETS 2023 is silent by scope and ASCO permits the G1–G2 menu on very low-quality consensus.
questions.proposal: The roadmap states no position on G3 hepatic debulking. positions.locator: What we are not sure about #19; Gate 6 · Standard 'Document somatostatin-receptor uptake…' · note

questions.question: Does the programme reproduce or restate the NCCN position against drug-eluting embolics, and on what basis?

positions.position: Advises against drug-eluting embolics in NET because they carry increased hepatobiliary toxicity in this population.
positions.locator: Gate 7 · Avoid 'Avoid drug-eluting embolics in NET.' · caveat

positions.position: Stopped on its safety endpoint: biloma in 7 of 13 (54%), two deaths. Roadmap critique: interrupted interim analysis, invisible beads with a tactile endpoint, injury in lowest-burden patients, rate out of line with other series.
positions.locator: Gate 7 · Avoid 'Avoid drug-eluting embolics in NET.' · caveat and note

positions.position: Reports that RETNET’s drug-eluting-bead arm closed for increased severe complications.
positions.locator: Gate 7 · Avoid 'Avoid drug-eluting embolics in NET.' · note

positions.position: Protocol paper only, with no outcome data; its power calculation assumed drug-eluting and lipiodol chemoembolisation equally safe, which the later arm closure contradicted.
positions.locator: What we are not sure about #15

questions.divergence: All sources point to avoidance, but the roadmap judges the basis thin, one 13-patient interim analysis plus an arm closure reported only in a guideline, so the position is precautionary rather than a demonstrated class effect.
questions.proposal: Keep the avoidance (Avoid, downgraded to grade C) and state its basis: a precautionary institutional choice, justified because the biliary harm is irreversible and two patients died, not a demonstrated class effect; use bland embolisation or conventional TACE instead. Any drug-eluting embolic use in NET is recorded as an exception with named approval.
questions.proposal_locator: Gate 7 · Avoid 'Avoid drug-eluting embolics in NET.' · pref and note; What we are not sure about #16; Decisions table #11 · audit
questions.rationale: The position is kept but it is a precautionary institutional choice, not a demonstrated class effect: a 13-patient interrupted interim analysis in which bilomas fell on the lowest-burden patients, with invisible beads and a tactile endpoint, and a biliary injury rate far out of line with other drug-eluting series. The confirmatory signal is an arm closure in an ongoing trial reported in a guideline. Stating the basis matters because the harm is irreversible and two patients died.
questions.audit: Audit: any drug-eluting embolic use in NET recorded as an exception with named approval.

questions.question: Which surveillance interval does the programme adopt for observed low-burden disease, and is observation documented as an equal alternative to an immediate analogue?
